evals.prompt: The design for our new billing webhook system is settled and was approved in last week's architecture review. The decision and the design doc live in docs/design/billing-webhooks.md. Give me an execution-ready implementation plan that an engineer can carry out without re-deriving the design.
evals.expected_output: A plan following the required structure: implementation objective, affected components/files (file-level), dependency ordering, interfaces/contracts affected, migration considerations with rollback, task breakdown with ownership, verification strategy per task, risks with mitigations, and unresolved assumptions. The plan stops at executable tasks and does not edit code.
assertions: Includes a single implementation objective statement
Lists affected components/files with concrete file or module names rather than vague areas
Contains a dependency ordering section describing which tasks precede others
Includes interfaces/contracts, migration considerations with rollback, task breakdown, verification strategy, and risks sections
Does not begin editing or writing code and states execution is handed to the implementation step

evals.prompt: We approved the auth token-refresh design in docs/design/auth-refresh.md last quarter, but since then we upgraded to FastAPI 0.110 and moved session storage to Redis. Produce an execution-ready implementation plan from that approved design.
evals.expected_output: A freshness/drift check that reports the material changes (FastAPI version, Redis session store) and their planning impact, followed by a full plan with the required sections grounded in the current repository state.
assertions: Reports a freshness/drift check identifying the changed repository state (FastAPI upgrade, Redis sessions)
Explains the planning impact of the drift before producing the plan
Produces the full required plan sections anchored to the current repo (not stale assumptions)
Avoids arbitrary file guesses not grounded in the actual repository

evals.prompt: I have a loose idea for a feature that lets users export all their data. I'm not sure what the behavior should be or which approach is best yet, but once we figure that out I want a build plan.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the requirements and chosen approach are still undecided and routes to requirements-and-design first; it does not produce an implementation plan or start coding.
assertions: States the requirements/approach are undecided and routes the work to requirements-and-design
Does not relitigate or produce a full execution plan
Does not begin writing or editing code

evals.prompt: Plan out how we should build the dark-mode feature.
evals.expected_output: The request has no mention of an approved design or recorded decision, so it is ambiguous between requirements-and-design (define what to build) and implementation-planning (plan the build). The agent asks a clarifying question or states the routing tie-breaker: it needs an approved design/decision first and otherwise routes to requirements-and-design/architecture-review.
assertions: Asks for clarification about whether an approved design or recorded decision exists, OR explicitly names the routing tie-breaker
States implementation-planning only plans from an already-approved design
Does not silently produce a plan or start implementation

evals.prompt: Thanks, the plan looks complete. Now go ahead and start implementing it — write the code for all the tasks in the plan.
evals.expected_output: The planning skill refuses to cross into implementation. It stops at the completed plan and hands execution to the implementation step, preserving scope and not editing code.
assertions: Refuses to begin editing or writing code as part of planning
States planning is complete and execution is handed to the implementation step
Does not relitigate the design or expand scope into implementation
